title: Pasta e Fagioli
subtitle: Italian bean and pasta soup
excerpt: This is a thick, hearty soup that sits somewhere between broth and stew. Blending half the beans gives the base body without needing cream or a roux, and the pancetta gives the whole pot a backbone of savour.
sourceNotes: Pasta e fagioli is a central Italian peasant dish that varies considerably by region -- northern versions tend to be thicker and creamier, while southern versions run brothier. The constant is the pairing of white beans and small pasta shapes.

content.text: Blending half the beans is the key step for texture -- it makes the soup naturally creamy without any added fat. Do this before the pasta goes in so the timing stays clean.

items.prepNote: small shapes such as ditalini or broken spaghetti

content.text: Heat the olive oil in the saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the pancetta and cook for 5 minutes until the fat has rendered. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 8 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and rosemary and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the tinned tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the drained cannellini beans and the chicken stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Scoop out roughly half the beans and blend them with a ladle of broth until smooth (use a jug blender or hand blender). Stir the puree back into the pot.
Add the pasta and cook until just tender, following the packet time. Taste for seasoning and loosen with a little water if the soup is very thick. Serve with a drizzle of olive oil.

items.symptom: Pasta has absorbed all the broth and turned to mush.
items.cause: Pasta was cooked too long or the soup was left to stand.
items.fix: Add hot water or stock to loosen and reheat gently. For make-ahead, cook the pasta separately and stir in per bowl.
